`default` is NOT a general floor, and should not be read as one. verify-gate
falls back to it only when the matched rules contributed NO commands at all
(verify-gate.sh:247), so with rules this broad the only way to reach it is a
turn that changes nothing but files inside the two `run: []` rules - in
practice a graphify-out-only or workflow-only turn. It is kept because those
are real turns and 7s of smoke is a better answer there than nothing.
There is deliberately no `always` key: any entry in it would make `cmds`
non-empty every time and `default` unreachable.
`seconds` is the rule's MEASURED cost, and it is the field verify-gate
reads for the Stop budget (verify.stopBudgetSeconds, default 60). It
replaces nothing: `why` keeps the reason, `seconds` carries the number,
because the costs used to live only as prose inside `why` ("8s", "29s",
"245s") and nothing could parse them. A rule with NO `seconds` is UNKNOWN
cost, which is NOT free: it always runs and the gate says its cost is
unstated. Most rules here are deliberately in that state - only the ones
actually timed carry a number, and filling the rest in by guesswork would

Cases 21-25 drive Install-Uv out of install-prerequisites.ps1 under pwsh, which closes a real gap: until 2026-09-22 ps-install-keys.sh was the ONLY committed check that ran the .ps1 and it SKIPs off Windows, so the .sh half had 49 cases and Install-Uv had none, and the Windows side shipped without the standalone-installer rung at all. 29s for the original six files; 96s (176 passed) measured end to end, alone with no other pytest process competing for CPU, on 2026-09-19 after two Codex/reviewer QA rounds on role-write-guard.sh/.ps1, role_write_guard.py and test_role_write_guard.py (all landed in crew 0.19.92, no version bump for either fix commit). Round 1 found 2 BLOCK + 4 FIX: role-write-guard.ps1's python resolver started as the same un-hardened one-liner pm-pulse.ps1's and verify-gate.ps1's own headers name as a bug, so it was replaced with a third byte-identical copy of Resolve-CrewPython; role-write-guard.sh's own resolver started as the shared, unfiltered `_common.sh` crew_py() and gained its own WindowsApps-stub rejection so the two shell flavours of this one hook cannot enforce different decisions on the same machine; a repo config that EXISTS but fails to parse (or whose `guards` key is not an object) now forces `block` rather than silently resolving to `off` (`crew_config.repo_config_is_corrupt`); scope is judged against the REAL, symlink/junction-resolved path, not the lexical one, closing a `.crew/link -> src/` escape (tested with an actual Windows junction via `mklink /J` and a POSIX symlink, both created for real on this machine, not simulated); `_normalise_role` strips only a leading `crew:` prefix rather than the last `:`-segment of anything, so `other-plugin:analyst` no longer collides with crew's own `analyst` deny-list entry; a non-object JSON payload or a non-string `file_path` degrades to 'cannot classify' instead of an uncaught exception exiting 1, which `PreToolUse` treats as a non-blocking pass-through; and `.crew/guard.log` now carries the `reason` column (`no-agent-type` / `unknown-role:<value>`) the module docstring already promised but the row-building code never wrote. Round 2 (a probe on the round-1 fix) found one more: `pm` writing OUTSIDE the repo entirely (the harness-sanctioned scratchpad) was refused, when this guard's whole purpose is the REPO's write scope -- fixed with `role_write_guard._is_outside_repo_lexically`, checked on the LEXICAL path only, never the symlink-resolved one, so a symlink staged inside `.crew/` pointing at an in-repo but out-of-scope directory stays refused by the round-1 real-path check rather than being swept into the new exception; confirmed with `os.path.islink` after bash's own `ln -s` silently fell back to a plain directory on this machine and produced a false pass. test_role_write_guard.py grew from 35 to 70 cases across four probe rounds. Round 3 (crew_config.repo_config_is_corrupt's sibling in the same commit series) redefined the outside-repo exception from role_write_guard._is_outside_repo_lexically (judged on the LEXICAL path, wrongly still refusing a symlink staged inside the repo whose target escapes it entirely) to role_write_guard._is_outside_repo (judged on the REAL resolved path, matching the in-scope check it sits beside), flipping two must-block cases to must-allow and adding a PowerShell/junction twin of the still-refused in-repo-out-of-scope case. Round 4, a PowerShell-security-hardening specialist review of role-write-guard.ps1, found and fixed four more: a launch failure (the resolved interpreter cannot actually be started) left $LASTEXITCODE null and `exit $LASTEXITCODE` silently evaluated to 0, so a restricted role's write went through unjudged -- fixed with a try/catch plus a null-exit-code check that falls back to a small PowerShell-side classification (deny-list + pm) only for THIS one failure mode; stdin was read via [Console]::In.ReadToEnd(), which decodes with the OEM codepage and silently mangles non-ASCII characters and a leading UTF-8 BOM, unlike role-write-guard.sh's byte-transparent read -- fixed by reading raw bytes, stripping a BOM, and forcing UTF-8 on the way back out through the pipe; Resolve-CrewPython never executed a candidate to prove it was real (role-write-guard.sh's resolver does) and `Get-Command -All` walked past a WindowsApps stub to a SAME-NAMED real python further down PATH, while bash's `command -v` takes only the first match per name and moves to the NEXT name -- so role-write-guard.ps1 now executes each candidate and mirrors the .sh's name-order exactly, which means it is DELIBERATELY no longer byte-identical to verify-gate.ps1's and pm-pulse.ps1's copies (a new two-way parity test plus a divergence tripwire replaced the old three-way one); and a missing role_write_guard.py exited 2 with a bare CPython file-not-found error, indistinguishable from a real block -- fixed with an explicit existence check and a crew-specific diagnostic, still exiting 2. PSScriptAnalyzer 1.25.0: zero findings both before and after. These hooks can BLOCK a turn, so CLAUDE.md requires must-block and must-allow cases. PROVEN by sabotage on 2026-09-13: reverting the Stop gate's baseline to `git diff --name-only HEAD` (the original bug) turns this rule red. A fifth round (7 BLOCK + 2 FIX) unified the config-corruption checks into crew_config.layer_state(path), applied to BOTH the repo and global config layers with an unconditional block-override; moved the stdin BOM strip and byte-level UTF-8 decoding into role_write_guard.py itself (shared by both shells); forced PYTHONUTF8=1 / PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 in the child environment from both shims; hardened the outermost exception handler against its own logging call raising a second exception; normalised a Windows extended-length path prefix before resolution; and added an exit-status check to role-write-guard.ps1's candidate probe. A sixth round (3 BLOCK + 1 FIX) fixed a dangling-symlink gap in layer_state (os.path.lexists replaces exists-or-isdir); gave role-write-guard.sh the same launch-failure fallback role-write-guard.ps1 got in round four; closed the most serious finding in this whole series (_resolve_real_target called os.path.abspath, which collapses .. lexically BEFORE resolving any symlink, so .crew/link/../app.py normalised to .crew/app.py -- in scope on the string alone -- while the OS resolves the symlink first and applies .. after, landing outside pm's scope; fixed with a component-wise walk that resolves symlinks as it goes and pops the RESOLVED parent for ..); and returned the outside-repo sentinel for a different-drive target instead of the generic cannot-classify answer. test_role_write_guard.py grew to 104 cases. Every fix across all six rounds was separately sabotage-tested on 2026-09-19 (28 mutations total across crew_config.py, role_write_guard.py, role-write-guard.sh and role-write-guard.ps1). One sabotage (the WindowsApps-stub-with-only-one-name-present case) was confirmed correct via repeated manual reproduction outside pytest but showed intermittent flakiness when run through pytest's own tmp_path fixture under sabotage specifically -- most likely Windows-Defender-style scan latency on rapidly created .cmd files, not a defect in the fix; the test itself passed reliably (dozens of runs) against the FIXED code throughout this session, each turning exactly its own must-block/must-allow cases red while every other case stayed green; each file was reverted to a byte-identical (sha256-verified) copy before committing. A seventh round, Codex round 4 on commit 3a0553a1, found the sixth round's own fix was right on POSIX and wrong on Windows: Win32 collapses a literal .. LEXICALLY before the filesystem/reparse-point layer ever sees it, so resolve-then-pop computed the opposite answer from real Windows in both directions (src/link/../new.py with link -> .crew/subdir wrongly allowed; .crew/link/../app.py with link -> src wrongly blocked), plus a separate gap where the walk split only on os.sep so a forward-slash target never walked a junction at all. _resolve_real_target now dispatches on os.name: _resolve_real_target_windows splits on both slash and backslash, collapses .. lexically first, then walks the ..-free path resolving junctions/symlinks; _resolve_real_target_posix is the original resolve-then-pop walk, unchanged, since that ordering is correct there. test_role_write_guard.py grew to 109 cases (108 passed, 1 skipped in 2.83s targeted / 31.85s full-file on 2026-09-19): one prior direct unit test of _resolve_real_target_posix was removed rather than forced to pass, because on this Windows machine that function's POSIX-rooted path arithmetic never matches a real disk path, os.path.lexists never fires true, and the walk silently degrades to pure lexical popping -- the exact bug being fixed, reproduced by the test harness rather than the code, which would have made a passing test prove nothing; real POSIX coverage is instead an end-to-end twin correctly skipped when os.name is nt. Both round-7 fixes sabotage-tested individually and reverted to sha256-verified byte-identical files: reverting the separator split flips exactly the 2 tests naming it; reverting the platform dispatch (forcing the POSIX algorithm everywhere) flips 3, including one pre-existing test that turned out to depend on the same dispatch for any native Windows-separator path, not just the .. cases. Full plugin/crew/tests/ suite on 2026-09-19, split to avoid test_verify_gate_lock_window.py's own documented contention flakiness: 1547 passed / 3 skipped / 36 deselected in 480.50s excluding that file, then test_verify_gate_lock_window.py alone, 36 passed in 229.01s -- 1583 passed, 3 skipped combined, run sequentially so neither part could contend with the other for CPU. Version stayed 0.19.92, no bump (round 4 was a fix-only round on an already-current version). An eighth round, Codex round 5 on commit 37bbf2ce, found the earlier extended-length-prefix fix (documented earlier in this same why field) was itself unsound: it normalised the Windows extended-length prefix away and classified the bare remainder, but that prefix exists specifically so Win32 skips its own path normalisation for that one call -- trailing dots and spaces are kept, a literal parent-directory dot-dot is never collapsed -- so stripping the prefix and classifying the remainder answers a question about a different path than the one Windows opens. Repro: an extended-length path naming .crew-dot (a trailing dot, a real distinct out-of-scope directory) under app.py stripped to a bare path ending in .crew-dot slash app.py, which this module then further normalised to end in plain .crew slash app.py -- in scope on the string alone -- while Windows opens .crew-dot itself, never plain .crew. Fixed by never classifying an extended-length path at all: a new detector short-circuits the main handler before repo-relative, real-repo-relative or classify ever run for such a path; pm and every deny-listed role fail closed unconditionally, every other role and a call with no agent_type allows, since Claude Code itself never emits this form for a Write or Edit call. test_role_write_guard.py grew to 114 cases: the must-block repro creates a REAL trailing-dot directory on disk via the same extended-length form, since an ordinary mkdir silently strips the trailing dot and collides with the already-existing .crew -- the test fixture itself needed the same fix the hook does. Two sabotages, both reverted to sha256-verified byte-identical files: inverting the restricted-role check flips exactly the 5 new tests; disabling detection entirely so the raw extended-length path falls through to the ordinary classifier flips only the 2 must-block cases and reproduces the exact original gap -- the 3 must-allow cases stay green either way, since an unrestricted role's write is not scope-checked regardless, itself useful confirmation the fix is scoped to restricted roles only. Full suite not re-run end to end for this round alone (unchanged since the prior 1583-passed measurement, which already covers this file); pylint 10.00/10, hooks/scripts/_test/run-tests.sh 75 passed, self-claims, sync-updates and smoke all green. check-marketplace.py reports exactly one finding on this branch -- plugin/crew/ has changed since version 0.19.92 was set at the version-swap commit, version not bumped -- confirmed by team-lead as the known squash-merge artefact also seen on items 1 and 3 (check_versions compares the version-set commit to HEAD, so a SECOND commit under one un-bumped version fails it by construction; the squash-merged commit on main lands version and content together and passes). Version stayed 0.19.92, no bump, per explicit instruction.

Re-time rather than trusting this figure too - it is a fact about one host on one day, not a rate. 1928s->377s is not a claimed 5x speedup of the SAME work: the earlier figure carries no host, so the two numbers are not known to describe comparable machines, and this entry deliberately does not assert they do. These four paths are imported by every test module, so a change here can make the whole suite vacuous while every module still reports green - the one case where nothing narrower is honest.
